title.en: The average and the group size

hints.en: `agg(["count", "mean"])` gives you both columns at once.

hints.tr: Tabloyu bir değişkene alıp `round(1)` uygula, sonra yazdır.
hints.en: Put the table in a variable, apply `round(1)`, then print it.

hints.tr: En küçük grup `tablo["count"].min()`, en yüksek ortalamalı şehir `tablo["mean"].idxmax()`.
hints.en: The smallest group is `table["count"].min()` and the city with the highest average `table["mean"].idxmax()`.

hints.tr:
Çözüm:

```python
tablo = data.groupby("city")["score"].agg(["count", "mean"]).round(1)

print(tablo)
print(tablo["count"].min())
print(tablo["mean"].idxmax())
print(tablo["mean"].idxmin())
```
hints.en:
The solution:

```python
table = data.groupby("city")["score"].agg(["count", "mean"]).round(1)

print(table)
print(table["count"].min())
print(table["mean"].idxmax())
print(table["mean"].idxmin())
```

hint.en: There is no `import pandas as pd` line.
